title: Polynomial augmentation has cotangent complex equal to the conormal module
statement: Let $n\geq0$, let $P=\mathbf Z[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, let $B=\mathbf Z$ with the augmentation $x_i\mapsto0$, and let $J=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$. For the standard cotangent complex of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence], there is a canonical isomorphism $L_{B/P}\simeq(J/J^2)[1]$ in $D(B)$. The classes of the $x_i$ form a $B$-basis of $J/J^2$, and the assertion includes the case $n=0$, where both sides are zero.

source.place: Tag 08SI (lemma-special-case), proof via the transitivity triangle, polynomial cotangent identification and the surjection conormal lemma.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-cotangent-transitivity-triangle] to the composable maps $\mathbf Z\to P\to B=\mathbf Z$. It gives the distinguished triangle $L_{P/\mathbf Z}\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}B\to L_{B/\mathbf Z}\to L_{B/P}\to(L_{P/\mathbf Z}\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}B)[1]$ in $D(B)$, with its canonical functoriality maps.

source.place: Tag 08QX (proposition-triangle), equation-triangle specialized to $\mathbf Z	o P	o\mathbf Z$.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-smooth-cotangent-identification] with base ring $\mathbf Z$ and the finite variable set $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, the first term is canonically $\Omega^1_{P/\mathbf Z}\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}B$. The differential module is free over $P$ on $\mathrm dx_1,\ldots,\mathrm dx_n$ by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables], hence is K-flat for this tensor calculation and its derived tensor with $B$ is the ordinary module $\Omega^1_{P/\mathbf Z}\otimes_PB$, free on $1\otimes\mathrm dx_i$.

source.place: Tag 08QH (polynomial cotangent complex) and algebra.tex Tag 00RX (polynomial differential basis).

proof.text: The middle term $L_{B/\mathbf Z}$ is zero: for the identity map $\mathbf Z\to\mathbf Z$, use the constant simplicial polynomial resolution in the definition of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence]. Its alternating-face complex is the constant module in degree zero with identity differentials in every positive even-to-odd pair, so the identity augmentation is a homotopy equivalence and the resulting cotangent complex is the zero object. This also covers $n=0$ without any separate convention.

source.place: Tags 08PN and 08QI, constant resolution calculation for the identity ring map.

proof.text: Rotating the triangle from Steps 1--3 and using the zero middle term identifies $L_{B/P}$ canonically with $(\Omega^1_{P/\mathbf Z}\otimes_PB)[1]$. The identification is the connecting morphism of that specified distinguished triangle, so it is canonical in the standard cotangent-complex construction.

source.place: Tag 08SI proof, displayed transitivity triangle after the polynomial and identity cotangent identifications.

proof.text: The sequence $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ is regular in $P=\mathbf Z[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$: successively quotienting by the preceding variables gives a polynomial ring over $\mathbf Z$, in which the next variable is a non-zero-divisor. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-conormal-free] identifies $J/J^2$ with the free $B$-module on the classes $[x_i]$. The differential-basis statement in Step 2 identifies $\Omega^1_{P/\mathbf Z}\otimes_PB$ with the free $B$-module on $1\otimes\mathrm dx_i$. Sending $1\otimes\mathrm dx_i$ to $[x_i]$ is thus a canonical $B$-linear isomorphism; shifting it by $[1]$ and composing with Step 4 gives the asserted canonical $L_{B/P}\simeq(J/J^2)[1]$. If $n=0$, both free modules have empty basis and are zero.
